style: Say playfully and cheerfully, like a fun music teacher
lines: Welcome to the Orchestra Zoo! Four instrument families live here. Tap a home to visit.
Who's playing? Press Listen, then tap the one you hear.
Welcome to the zoo band! Pick a melody, a bass and a beat. Then press Play the band.
Welcome to the string family! We make music with strings that shake. Pull a bow across them, or pluck them with your fingers.
Hoo! Welcome to the woodwind family. Blow air into a tube. Some woodwinds have a thin reed that buzzes.
Welcome to the brass family! Buzz your lips into a metal mouthpiece: bzzzz! The tubes make it loud and bright.
Welcome to the percussion family! Hit it, shake it or scrape it. Some play notes, some just keep the beat.
The violin is the smallest string instrument, so it plays the highest notes. Its bow is strung with horse hair!
You sit down to play the cello. It stands on the floor between your knees and sings low and warm.
The double bass is taller than a grown-up! It is the biggest, so it plays the lowest string notes.
A concert harp has 47 strings. You pluck them with your fingers. Long strings are low, short strings are high.
The flute has no reed. You blow across a hole, like blowing over the top of a bottle.
The oboe has two reeds tied together that buzz. The whole orchestra tunes to the oboe's note.
The clarinet has one reed that buzzes against the mouthpiece. It can play very low and very high.
The saxophone is made of metal, but it is a woodwind because it uses a reed. Surprise!
The bassoon's tube is almost 9 feet long, folded in half. It plays the lowest woodwind notes.
The trumpet is the smallest brass instrument and plays the highest. Press its 3 valves to change the notes.
The trombone has a slide instead of valves. Slide it out for lower notes, in for higher notes.
The French horn's tube is curled in circles. Stretched out straight, it would be about 12 feet long!
The tuba is the biggest brass instrument, so it plays the lowest brass notes. Oom-pah!
A metal bar bent into a triangle. Ting! Hold it by the string so it can ring.
A giant metal plate. One soft hit makes a sound that swirls and shimmers for a long time.
Crash two metal plates together. CRASH! Then they shimmer.
Timpani are big kettle drums that play real notes. A pedal makes the drumhead tighter for higher notes.
Wires under the snare drum rattle when you hit it. Rat-a-tat-tat!
The bass drum is so big you can feel its BOOM in your tummy.
Hit the wooden bars with mallets. Short bars play high notes, long bars play low notes.
Shake it or tap it. The little metal jingles go jingle-jingle!
Press a key and a little hammer hits a string inside. So the piano is a bit percussion and a bit strings!
Listen from smallest to biggest. Do the notes get higher or lower? The bigger the instrument, the lower it sounds.
Listen to every member of the percussion family, one after another.
Did you hear it? The bigger the instrument, the lower it sounds.
That was the whole percussion family!
Listen. Which family is playing?
Listen. Which instrument is playing?
Listen. Which strings instrument is it?
Listen. Which woodwinds instrument is it?
Listen. Which brass instrument is it?
Listen. Which percussion instrument is it?
Not that one. Listen again!
Yes! It's the violin, from the strings family.
Yes! It's the cello, from the strings family.
Yes! It's the double bass, from the strings family.
Yes! It's the harp, from the strings family.
Yes! It's the flute, from the woodwinds family.
Yes! It's the oboe, from the woodwinds family.
Yes! It's the clarinet, from the woodwinds family.
Yes! It's the saxophone, from the woodwinds family.
Yes! It's the bassoon, from the woodwinds family.
Yes! It's the trumpet, from the brass family.
Yes! It's the trombone, from the brass family.
Yes! It's the French horn, from the brass family.
Yes! It's the tuba, from the brass family.
Yes! It's the triangle, from the percussion family.
Yes! It's the gong, from the percussion family.
Yes! It's the cymbals, from the percussion family.
Yes! It's the timpani, from the percussion family.
Yes! It's the snare drum, from the percussion family.
Yes! It's the bass drum, from the percussion family.
Yes! It's the xylophone, from the percussion family.
Yes! It's the tambourine, from the percussion family.
Yes! It's the piano, from the percussion family.
